Vocations.name: Vocations
Vocations.text:
A deity may call upon their followers for more than just the traditional measures of their worship, but instead on a specific role the follower is meant to fill as their devotee, and you have heard this calling. This requires you to take on additional edicts and anathema that are adjoined with your vocation, and in exchange, you are afforded certain luxuries that other followers are not.

Your vocation symbolizes your main mission as a cleric, so you can only have one vocation. Some deities may not have vocations of a certain kind or actively discourage certain vocations (such as a heretic for Torag who forbids lies or clinician for Zon-Kuthon). Other servitor’s of your deity may consider your methods unorthodox despite following their deity given your differences from the standard followers of the faith, and as such may not be helpful towards you despite sharing the same deity.

Vocation, Vocation, Vocation

Your vocation symbolizes your main mission as a cleric, so you can only have one vocation. Some deities may not have vocations of a certain kind or actively discourage certain vocations (such as a heretic for Torag who forbids lies or clinician for Zon-Kuthon). Other servitor’s of your deity may consider your methods unorthodox despite following their deity given your differences from the standard followers of the faith, and as such may not be helpful towards you despite sharing the same deity.Clerics are the pivotal class for the design of a vocation, as a vocation often requires dedication that only a studious and focused member of the clergy can afford. However, it might make sense to apply the aspects of a vocation to other classes that rely on deities, such as a champion. In doing so, it’s important that measures are taken to illustrate the sacrifices needed to fulfill a vocation. For instance, if a non-cleric class with a vocation would have proficiency in martial weapons and the deities weapon is martial, you should exclude the benefits listed under the favored weapon entry, or alternatively, remove that class’s proficiency in martial weapons to compensate. Each vocation should require a class to give up something meaningful to attain its benefits.

Using Vocations

To use vocations simply drag the @UUID[Compendium.clerics-remaster.clerics-paragon-vocation.aD5mvFBh7NOQ7T7D]{Vocations} class feature into your character sheet. Denomonations.text:
The deities of Golarion are not physical beings with the same sets of rules as mortals; they are ephemeral, mysterious beings open to countless interpretations. For example, in colder climates, followers of Sarenrae worship her as Sister Cinder, goddess of the hearth. Intro.name: Intro
Intro.text:
Foreward

Remastering Clerics+ has been a blessing, and has taught us many things. This was the 3rd book we released as Team+. By then, we had started to feel more comfortable in exploring with our designs. This was the first book to feature a Team+ “Ion” in Vocations, a mechanic used to modify the deity stat block. Lucky for us, Clerics worked perfectly as the birthplace of the Ion, and it allowed us to create a cleric who could serve their god in a special way. The new remaster design of Cleric did a lot to bring the warpriest doctrine into a wonderful new light but we still felt that the newly named “Paragon” class archetype made for interesting take on being a divine martial. The Seeker doctrine reinvisioned from its previous identity to a new one more grounded in flavor, while armorclad serves as an alternate warpriest. We also tuned up language and mechanics to our current standards across the board. Thank you to those who supported us by already having this book, and thank you to any new members of Fam+. We’re proud of this book and we hope that you enjoy.

Clerics+

The work of the devout is never done, for their toils and tasks are as endless as the power of the beings they serve. Clerics convey their constancy through acts of service to their deity; Acts that can take many forms. Whether it be study, battle, a profession of faith, or simply the recovery of something lost, those of the cloth heed when asked and do so without wavering. A god's call is not simply a request but a divine proclamation which requires an answer. Only those voices with cultivated discernment, pious spirituality, and passionate fidelity are chosen to respond by becoming a clergy of the church.

Clerics+ in Foundry VTT

Unlike many other Team+ Books, the Clerics+ Module does not use a custom class sheet. To use the options presented in this book, you start by building a @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.classes.EizrWvUPMS67Pahd]{Cleric} as normal. To utilize the Vocations or Paragon Class Archetype, you must manually add @UUID[Compendium.clerics-remaster.clerics-paragon-vocation.aD5mvFBh7NOQ7T7D]{Vocations} or @UUID[Compendium.clerics-remaster.clerics-paragon-vocation.RoVbvF6mqwHEnzib]{Sacred Decree} into your character sheet as normal.

For bug reports or inquires, please message @lyon_naglfar on the official Team+ discord. https://discord.com/invite/yHQbmVzDfR

New Doctrines.name: New Doctrines
New Doctrines.text:
Throughout Golarion, different people take on their faith in different ways. Some are interested in divine magic; others are more concerned with wading into danger to aid others, and some become involved in the interests and intrigues of the churches themselves. Below is the new seeker doctrine and an alternate doctrine for the warpriest doctrine named the armorclad.

@UUID[Compendium.clerics-remaster.clerics-features.SEOIqUhV5SHGJPuM]{Seeker}

You are an agent of the church, tasked with seeking out the interests of your faith; lost knowledge, abandoned relics, enemies of your god and heretics within the flock itself.

Where There's a Will

The new version of the seeker doctrine is designed to be a devout member of the church whose role is orchestrated according to the will of their deity. The will of your deity may speak to you profoundly and often, it may whisper, or it may not even speak at all but instead uses signs to convey its will. Whatever the method of communication, seekers pursue their deity’s immediate whims as their primary purpose.

@UUID[Compendium.clerics-remaster.clerics-features.pIHDsn6Cw43JzzuN]{First Doctrine}

You’re trained in light armor, and you have expert proficiency in Perception. You gain the @UUID[Compendium.clerics-remaster.clerics-actions.Z1OhAfxlOY718JP3]{Seek the Will} action. At 5th level when you would gain the perception expertise class feature, you instead gain expert proficiency in Reflex saves and at 11th level when you would gain the reflex expertise class feature, you instead become expert in Fortitude saves. At 13th level, if you gain the divine defense class feature, you also gain expert proficiency in light armor.

@UUID[Compendium.clerics-remaster.clerics-features.pLVOxBIvzFPPjFf3]{Second Doctrine}

You gain the @UUID[Compendium.clerics-remaster.clerics-actions.yq3ipSNC3UJQW6C9]{Wield the Will} action.

@UUID[Compendium.clerics-remaster.clerics-features.A0QWYwQhBNOOnP4y]{Third Doctrine}

You gain expert proficiency with your deity's favored weapon, simple weapons, and unarmed attacks. When you make a Strike using your result from Wield the Will, you deal an additional 1d4 spirit damage. When you critically succeed at an attack roll using these weapons, you apply the weapon’s critical specialization effect; you can use your spell DC in place of your class DC.

@UUID[Compendium.clerics-remaster.clerics-features.Qz8u5Q9AeyDlJq3E]{Fourth Doctrine}

Your proficiency ranks for the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics to expert.

@UUID[Compendium.clerics-remaster.clerics-features.FNkegnV0CQ5PwV1s]{Fifth Doctrine}

Your proficiency rank in Perception increases to master. Your Perception DC to lie to you increases by 2 and you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Sense Motive and to see through disguises.

@UUID[Compendium.clerics-remaster.clerics-features.FZ8h6Qgaw6pFaXfV]{Final Doctrine}

You gain master proficiency with your deity’s favored weapon, simple weapons, unarmed attacks, spell attack modifier, and spell DC. The additional spirit damage to your Strikes when you use the result of your Wield the Will increases to 2d4.

@UUID[Compendium.clerics-remaster.clerics-features.ChqvhQ15pjXPvTtj]{Armorclad (Alternate Warpriest)}

You follow your deity’s will into places of danger, combining divine protection with sacred steel to protect you from all threats. This doctrine functions as the warpriest doctrine for prerequisites and for the purposes of abilities that function based on your doctrine.

Doctrine Deviation

The armorclad is an alternate option for the warpriest doctrine which leans into a more defensive nature than the original doctrine. When selecting feats or options, such as the Paragon class archetype, the armorclad and warpriests doctrines can be used interchangeably for the purposes of selection and prerequisites.

@UUID[Compendium.clerics-remaster.clerics-features.OFD8u3hatprr3r2C]{First Doctrine}

You’re trained in light, medium and heavy armor, simple weapons and martial weapons of your deity’s favored weapon group, and your deity’s favored weapon if it is advanced. You also gain the Shield Block general feat. If your deity’s weapon is simple, you gain the Deadly Simplicity cleric feat. At 13th level, if you gain the divine defense class feature, you also gain expert proficiency in light, medium, and heavy armor.

@UUID[Compendium.clerics-remaster.clerics-features.u3r7QE1I93HgSEH1]{Second Doctrine}

Your proficiency rank for Fortitude saves increases to expert.

@UUID[Compendium.clerics-remaster.clerics-features.DAVyD2vGoSV5OiuM]{Third Doctrine}

You gain expert proficiency with unarmed attacks, simple weapons, and martial weapons of your deity’s favored weapon group, and your deity’s favored weapon if it is advanced. When you critically succeed at an attack roll using these weapons, you apply the weapon’s critical specialization effect; you can use your spell DC in place of your class DC.

@UUID[Compendium.clerics-remaster.clerics-features.BlvO3unU7e70Nfos]{Fourth Doctrine}

Your proficiency ranks for the spell attack modifier and spell DC statistics to expert.

@UUID[Compendium.clerics-remaster.clerics-features.3vKoRbcYaHuLHG5K]{Fifth Doctrine}

Your proficiency rank for Fortitude saves increases to master. When you roll a success at a Fortitude save, you get a critical success instead.

@UUID[Compendium.clerics-remaster.clerics-features.0xfTdMaE8Opr4ehS]{Final Doctrine}

You gain master proficiency with unarmored, light, medium, and heavy armor, spell attack modifier, and spell DC.

Paragon Class Archetype.name: Paragon Class Archetype
Paragon Class Archetype.text:
Some clerics are tasked with an even greater mission than others in the clergy. Granted a sacred decree marked directly into their body, these noble battle-preachers manifest their divine magic not through spells, but through sanctified powers of the body, the mind and the spirit. The path to becoming a paragon varies from church to church; in some churches, they are selected from applicants who have vowed to undertake a holy mission. In others, these chosen ones are forced to become a mirror of their god by wicked priests. No matter the path, paragons emerge as lesser heralds of their god—with the possibility of ascending to greater heights in the future.

@UUID[Compendium.clerics-remaster.clerics-paragon-vocation.RoVbvF6mqwHEnzib]{Sacred Decree}

You have been given specific guidance on what you must do for your god, a sacred decree bound into your mortal form. This decree blesses you with additional powers that are reserved for those that take on the role of a gerald of your god, and is determined by your cleric doctrine. You must select @UUID[Compendium.clerics-remaster.clerics-feats.gHBCdWldQU3UQlHz]{Paragon Dedication} as your 2nd-level class feat.

@UUID[Compendium.clerics-remaster.clerics-features.jhVSW51oaIf4mLi7]{Decree of Might}

Prerequisites @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.classfeatures.0Aocw3igLwna9cjp]{Warpriest} doctrine

Your deity has blessed your body, binding you to battle as an ever constant testament to your journey as a herald of your deity. Paragons of might are most common among deities who call clerics to fight, from being called to competitive bouts as a cleric of Irori or constantly striving to achieve justice under the banner of Iomedae. Your arms serve as your scripture, and its words are written in the many dents and stains it collects during your tenure as a paragon.

@UUID[Compendium.clerics-remaster.clerics-features.Em8MYX1hWLhTq5yI]{First Decree (1st)}

Your key ability attribute is either Strength or Dexterity. You gain your second doctrine at 1st level instead of 3rd. When you would gain the benefits of your second doctrine, you instead gain the Emblazon Armament cleric feat or another class feat to which you have access if you already possessed Emblazon Armament.
